dedupe_keys.name: encuesta nacional de hospitales venezuelan hospital national survey 2018 selection

description: This survey records the working condition of hospitals across Venezuela in March 2018. The producers are groups of Venezuelan doctors who ran the National Hospital Survey through a shared crowdsourced questionnaire; OCHA's Latin America and Caribbean office published this selection on the Humanitarian Data Exchange. Coverage is national, with about 136 public and private hospitals across the states. Each response names the hospital, state, city and administering body and rates water supply in the previous week, the status of X-ray, ultrasound, CT scanning and the clinical laboratory, meal service, shortages of medicines and supplies that patients must buy, and other services, using categories such as fully operational, intermittent failures or not operational. The file is available as a free XLSX download under a Creative Commons Attribution licence. Caveats: responses are self-reported by volunteer doctors, not audited, only one round from 2018 is included, column names are in Spanish, and the selection may not cover every hospital. Simulation uses: evidence of how utility failures, especially water, cascade into loss of hospital services, calibrating degraded-capacity states for hospital resilience models, and prioritising support to hospitals. Related records: the Syria Ministry of Health hospital list (data-syria-moh-hospitals-status) gives operational status in another crisis setting.
